description: The identifier's own structure says the object is not the paper. Above admission (`replication-claim`, 700): a review object echoes its parent's title verbatim, so it fires replication arms on something that is not the study, and no amount of replication vocabulary in the text makes the identifier point at a paper. Four separately-labelled arms, kept as their own clauses so each can be audited and retired on its own evidence. (1) A `/reviews/` or `/decisions/` path segment is minted by the publisher for the review object (e.g. 10.7287/peerj.10325v0.1/reviews/2); such records echo the reviewed paper's title verbatim, so every replication phrase in the title fires on something that is not the paper. A narrowing worth doing later is anchoring the segment to known registrants rather than matching anywhere in the DOI. (2) A DOI ending in `.suppl` is the supplementary object minted alongside an article, not the article; terminal-anchored so it cannot fire on a DOI that merely contains the string. It is the identifier-side counterpart of the `supplementary-materials` work type in not-a-report-type, and the two overlap deliberately: different fields, either one alone is enough. (3) PCI Registered Reports encodes the same two objects as SUFFIXES on the reviewed paper's own DOI instead of as path segments: `.rev11`, `.rev12`, `.d1`. The arm is anchored to that one registrant, because a bare `\.d\d+$` is too generic to apply to the whole corpus while `10.24072` is a single publisher whose scheme can be stated exactly. It overlaps the `review of:` / `decision revise:` title arms of not-a-paper-title deliberately: different fields, either one alone is enough. (4) The PCI recommendation itself carries the bare DOI, `10.24072/pci.<community>.<number>`, and the authors' reply to the reviewers adds `.arN`. A recommendation is a review object that Crossref links to the reviewed preprint through `relation.is-review-of` (1,399 of the 1,400 counted; the other carries `is-comment-on`). It is not the study, and it is not redirected to the preprint either: for all five Registered Reports recommendations checked, the relation points at an OSF or PsyArXiv URL rather than a DOI. PCI Registered Reports reviews the manuscript itself, often an OSF file with no DOI (the creativity–depression Stage 2 manuscript is a .docx), so no DOI exists to redirect to. All five reviewed studies are in the pool as their own works, as preprints or as the published articles (e.g. 10.1525/collabra.122515 for the creativity–depression study, 10.1037/xlm0001424 for the irrelevant-speech study). Four of the five are Stage 1 recommendations of a protocol. not-a-paper-abstract reaches the recommendations whose abstract opens 'A recommendation of:'; this arm reaches the rest, whose abstract is the recommender's own text. Peer Community Journal articles (`10.24072/pcjournal.`) are papers and do not match. Deposit-only registrants are a different kind of claim — a list of external facts about who mints what, not a pattern in the identifier — and live in their own spec, `deposit-registrant`.

measured.rationale: Arm 1 (/reviews/ | /decisions/), carried unchanged from the retired `non-article-doi` spec: a DOI path segment minted by the publisher for the review object itself, so the mapping is structural, not statistical.

Arm 2 (\.suppl$), new in the v2 rule book: a terminal ".suppl" is the identifier a publisher mints for the supplementary object of an article. Structural for the same reason as arm 1 — the claim is about what the registrant writes into the identifier, not about a rate estimated from a sample — and the terminal anchor is what keeps it that way: a DOI that merely contains the string is not claimed.

Arm 3 (^10.24072/….revN|.dN), issue #192. Structural in the same sense as arm 1 — the suffix is what PCI Registered Reports mints for the review and decision objects of the paper whose DOI it is extended from — and the registrant anchor is what keeps it that way. Count over a named population: 66 works in the 5,146,160-row survivor pool carry such a DOI, and every one of the 66 titles was read: 42 begin 'Review of:' and 24 'Decision Revise:', and none is a study. Recall against data/flora.csv is exact: 0 of its 2,504 doi_r and 0 of its doi_o values match.

Arm 4 (^10.24072/pci.<community>.N, optionally .arN). Structural, and confirmed by a full count over the registrant on 2026-10-28: Crossref holds 4,407 records under 10.24072. Of these, 1,400 carry the bare shape across 29 PCI communities (Registered Reports 264), and 1,399 of the 1,400 carry `relation.is-review-of`. The remaining one, 10.24072/pci.evolbiol.100019, is a recommendation of a published Cell article and carries `is-comment-on` instead. A further 573 carry `.arN`, the authors' replies. The 650 Peer Community Journal articles (10.24072/pcjournal.*) do not match. Recall against data/flora.csv is exact: 0 of its doi_r and 0 of its doi_o values match. The FLoRA entry sheet does list eight such DOIs as doi_r. They are errors in the sheet, reported in forrtproject/fred-data#152.
